headline: Ombudsman Dismisses Former BFP Chief, Files Bribery and Graft Charges Over ₱485M Ambulance Deal
seoTitle: Ombudsman Dismisses Former BFP Chief Over Ambulance Deal | FMB News
seoDescription: The Ombudsman dismissed former BFP chief Jesus Fernandez from government service and filed bribery and graft charges over a ₱485-million ambulance procurement.
deck: The anti-graft office said its investigation found grounds to administratively dismiss Jesus Fernandez and bring criminal charges tied to the procurement of 132 ambulances. The criminal allegations remain for the courts to determine.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Office of the Ombudsman has dismissed former Bureau of Fire Protection chief Jesus Fernandez from government service and filed criminal charges against him before the Sandiganbayan over an ambulance procurement worth about ₱485 million.

The Ombudsman said Fernandez faces two counts of indirect bribery and two counts of violation of Section 3(b) of Republic Act No. 3019, the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act. Rosaverna Sangga, identified as the representative of the joint venture involved in the procurement, was also charged with two counts of corruption of public officials.

In a separate administrative case, the Ombudsman found Fernandez guilty of grave misconduct and conduct prejudicial to the best interest of the service. The administrative penalty includes dismissal, cancellation of eligibility, forfeiture of retirement benefits and perpetual disqualification from reemployment in government service.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The case grew out of a complaint filed by the Department of the Interior and Local Government after a fact-finding investigation into the procurement of 132 Type 1 Basic Life Support ambulances.

The procurement contract was awarded to Toyota Mabolo, which entered into a joint venture with Autozone Prime Distributors Inc. The Ombudsman said its investigation alleged that Fernandez received a total of ₱14.752 million on two occasions, including ₱10.752 million in November 2024 and ₱4 million in September 2025.

The September 3 action is materially different from the earlier stage of the controversy in March, when the DILG had filed complaints with the Ombudsman. The anti-graft office has now issued an administrative ruling and brought criminal charges to the Sandiganbayan.

sections.heading: Why this matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: The case concerns procurement for emergency medical vehicles funded through government spending, making the integrity of the bidding and purchasing process a direct public-interest issue.

The Ombudsman’s administrative ruling is already an official action, while the criminal charges will still have to be tested in court. Filing charges does not establish criminal guilt, and Fernandez is entitled to due process and the presumption of innocence.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: The next material developments include the Sandiganbayan’s handling of the criminal cases, any plea or defense filed by Fernandez and Sangga, and whether either party challenges the Ombudsman’s administrative ruling through available legal remedies.
FMB News will also watch for any additional official findings concerning the ambulance procurement, the supplier arrangement or other officials who may be named in related proceedings.

verificationNotes: The central event was corroborated independently by Philippine News Agency, GMA News and INQUIRER.net, all citing the Office of the Ombudsman’s September 3 action.
The article distinguishes the Ombudsman’s administrative finding from the criminal charges now before the Sandiganbayan and does not present criminal guilt as established.
The March 2026 DILG complaint was treated as background rather than a new event; the September 3 Ombudsman ruling and filing of criminal charges are the material new developments.
